content:
Thoughts on using multiple Signal devices simultaneously? The encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to an existing Signal account, instead of being limited to only iPads as a second mobile device.

Alongside today's announcement of Android-linked functionality, the company stated: "We are also expanding linked device support on iOS, so in addition to the iPad we have always supported, you can now link an iPhone to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can selectively transfer their full message history along with media saved over the past 45 days.

Signal says the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption, employing the same "link-and-sync" technology already available on iPad and desktop devices, including the Mac version of Signal.

This expanded support is particularly useful for anyone who uses two separate iPhones for work and personal use, or who needs to test multiple devices.

The move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to that of the Apple Messages ecosystem, where users can seamlessly carry on conversations across iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Signal for iOS version 8.22 is coming soon to the App Store. Signal has previously introduced a username feature, allowing people to connect without sharing their phone number.
